Why go: pink dolphins and Pig Island in one day

The "pink dolphins" of the Gulf of Thailand are Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins (Sousa chinensis). They are born dark grey and lose pigment as they age, so adults turn pale pink or mottled pink and white. A resident group of more than 50 lives along the mainland coast of Khanom district in Nakhon Si Thammarat province, south-west of Koh Samui, feeding in the shallow bays around Laem Prathap and Ao Kwang Phao. The species is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, and it is one of the few dolphins you can see on a day trip from Samui.

This tour combines a dolphin search with our classic southern islands. A shared speedboat crosses about 45 minutes of open water to the dolphins' usual feeding grounds, where a captain who knows the area looks for them, then returns to snorkel the shallow reef at Koh Tan (about 45 minutes in the water) and spend about an hour with the pigs on Koh Madsum (Pig Island). Lunch and fruit are included, and the day lasts about 6 hours. The order of stops depends on tide, wind and where the dolphins are that morning.

Be realistic. The dolphins are wild animals. Sightings are common but never guaranteed, and some days they stay out of sight. We don't chase, feed or surround them, and there is no refund if none are seen. The Koh Tan and Koh Madsum stops are the guaranteed part of the day. If the pigs and a snorkel are all you want, the Pig Island speedboat tour does that for 1,450 THB in 4–5 hours.

Watching dolphins responsibly

  • The captain slows down well before the dolphins and keeps a respectful distance.
  • The boat never chases, cuts across or circles a group, and goes to neutral or switches off when dolphins come close.
  • No swimming with the dolphins and no feeding. In Khanom, fish sold at piers for feeding changes their behaviour and can make them ill.
  • Stay seated and quiet; sudden movement and noise send them down.

Who this tour is for

  • Wildlife lovers who accept that sightings depend on the day.
  • Families with children aged about 6 and over, who can manage a longer open-water crossing.
  • Photographers with a zoom lens: dolphins surface briefly and at a distance.
  • Travellers who have already seen Pig Island and want more from the south-west coast.

Who should choose another tour

  • Only want the pigs and a snorkel: the speedboat tour or the longtail tour.
  • Get seasick easily: the 45-minute open-water crossing is the roughest part of any Pig Island trip; choose the longtail, which stays in sheltered water.
  • Pregnant or with back problems: we don't advise the speedboat.
  • Want your own boat and timing: the Pig Island private speedboat.
  • Travelling with toddlers: the shorter Pig Island trips are easier.

What to bring

  • Binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens.
  • Polarised sunglasses: they help you spot dolphins under the surface glare.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen and a hat that ties on.
  • Swimwear, a towel and a change of clothes.
  • Cash in small notes for the Koh Madsum island fee (about 50 THB per person) and drinks or snacks on the islands.
  • A dry bag or phone pouch, sandals and a copy of your passport.
  • Seasickness tablets if you need them.

Good to know

  • Best months: February to September, when the sea is flatter and dolphins are easier to spot at the surface. October to December is rainy and windier; the trip runs when the sea is safe, but sightings are harder in chop. If we cancel for weather, you choose a full refund or a new date.
  • Time of day: dolphins feed most actively in the morning, which is why this trip starts early.
  • Seasickness: sit towards the back of the boat, look at the horizon and avoid a heavy breakfast.
  • Mobility: boarding may involve stepping down from a pier or wading at a beach; there are no climbs.
  • Children: children's life jackets are provided and children wear them at all times on the boat.
  • The pigs: watch and photograph, let them come to you, don't chase, lift or feed them junk food.
  • Drones: don't fly over the dolphins. Elsewhere, registered drones only (CAAT and NBTC), and ask the captain first.

Pickup and meeting point

Transfers to the pier are included from the main areas of Koh Samui: Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem. Remote areas cost 400 THB per person return; the booking card shows any surcharge for your area. The van ride to the pier takes about 30 minutes from most hotels, longer from Maenam and the north coast. Pickup is in the morning, and we send your exact time by 18:00 the day before. If the van can't reach your road, we send a nearby meeting point with a map pin.
